title: feat(spec): the protocol declares what an ABSENT `scale` means per field type — `percent` means 0
body:
Fixes #19579

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Executes the maintainer ruling recorded on `objectstack-ai/objectui` `issuecomment-5749111840` (director seat, summon 25, batch 194 item 1, **letter A′**, 「同意」), quoted rather than paraphrased:

> `@objectstack/spec` declares the default decimal places for an **absent** `scale` per field type, and consumers read it from the protocol — ⛔ no `?? N` in any consumer. **percent ⇒ 0** in this card.

This is the `@objectstack/spec` half only. Removing the consumer fallbacks is `objectstack-ai/objectui#9843`, which declares this card its blocker and must not land before it.

## What lands

- **`resolveFieldScale(field)`** — new, in `packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.ts`, exported through `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`. It answers the **effective** decimal width: the field's declared `scale` when it has a well-formed one, otherwise the platform's declared value for an absent `scale` on that field type, otherwise `undefined` ("no fixed width"). `percent` is the one type with a declared value, and it is **0**.
- **`FieldScaleMeta`** — the metadata subset the width is resolvable from. `scale` is typed `unknown` deliberately: renderers reach this helper with loose stored metadata where a `scale` arriving as a string is real, and inventing a width from a string is the consumer-side guessing the platform refuses.
- **`FieldSchema.scale`'s `.describe()`** now states the rule in words an author can read and names the resolver as the single source — the ③ facet of the ruling. The generated field reference page carries it (three pages, five rows, regenerated).
- A `minor` changeset on `@objectstack/spec`.

Returning the effective width rather than only the absent value is what makes the ⛔ half reachable: a helper that answered only "what does absence mean" would leave every call site writing `field.scale ?? resolver(field)`, which is a `?? N` in a consumer by another spelling.

## Which of the two `scale` declarations the ruling means — established, not assumed

`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` carries **two**. The card names one, and the answer is `FieldSchema.scale`:

| declaration | what it is | reachable for `percent`? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FieldSchema.scale` (`field.zod.ts:1226` at the base of this branch) | a field's displayed/entered decimal width | yes — this is the ruling's subject |
| `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale` (`:931`) | decimal places to round a **computed** grid cell result to, before `toFixed` | no — that schema's own `type` enum is `text · number · currency · date · datetime · time · select · lookup · file`, with no `percent` member, so `percent ⇒ 0` has no landing there |

They also answer different questions (a display width vs the rounding of a platform-computed value), so the grid-column key is left untouched rather than given a pointer it would have to keep in step.

## Shape measured first

`FieldSchema` is a **flat** `strictObject` inside a `lazySchema`, with type applicability expressed by a `superRefine` and type-conditional defaults materialized in an `.overwrite()` tail — ⛔ **not** a per-type union. Per the card that means one exported resolver, and that is what this is. Two independent measurements say the schema is the wrong instrument:

1. **A key-level `.default(0)` cannot see `type`** and would land on every numeric type at once. That is plain letter **A**, refused by name in the ruling because an undeclared currency would fall from `$25.00` to `$25`.
2. **A type-conditional `.overwrite()` materialization — which *can* see `type`, and is what `unique` and `deleteBehavior` already do in this file — is still wrong, for a reason outside presentation entirely.** `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts:789` gates the write-time `max_scale` **refusal** on `def.scale !== undefined`. Materializing a `0` would arm that refusal on every percent field whose author declared nothing (allowance `scale + 2` on a fraction-stored percent, exactly `scale` on a whole-percent one) — turning writes the platform accepts today into writes it rejects. That is a stored-data change bought for a display ruling, and one no author could read off their own metadata.

⇒ the absent value stays **absent on the parsed field** and is resolved at the moment of display. A pin asserts that: `FieldSchema.parse({ name, label, type: 'percent' })` produces output with no `scale` key, and `resolveFieldScale` still answers `0` for it. `check:authorable-surface` is green and `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/` is unchanged, which is the same fact from the ratchet's side — no key gained a default, so nothing needed a `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR` declaration.

## The census: `number` and `currency` do NOT ride this PR

The card admits them only if a consumer census shows one consistent absent-value per type. **Neither census produced one, and the two failed differently** — `number`’s consumers **disagree** (one face resolves absence to no fixed width, three resolve it to 0), while for `currency` **no display face reads the key at all** while the write path still enforces it. Under the card’s own instruction each therefore takes its own card with the readings. Measured in `objectstack-ai/objectui` at `origin/main` `0cf2d6644bdb96a9a6784ef801ee6a60a5306bd8`, and re-read identically at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `87af769e9a3ee28ace099fdd653d3ebd79fe82e2` — both trees agree line for line:

| site | absent `scale` resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:844` — `PercentCellRenderer` | `0` |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx:1233` — detail summary chip | `0` |
| `packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts:343` and `:401` — grid summary footer | `0` |
| `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectMetricWidget.tsx:229` — metric widget | `0` |
| `packages/fields/src/widgets/PercentField.tsx:116` — the percent EDIT widget | **`2`** |
| `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:772-773` — `NumberCellRenderer` | **no fixed width** (minimum 0, maximum 20) |

- **percent — CONSISTENT at `0`.** Every percent-specific read face resolves `0`; the single outlier is the edit widget's `2`, and its own comment already records the disagreement as awaiting exactly this ruling: 「that leaves this widget and `PercentCellRenderer` still disagreeing when nothing is declared … Whether the two faces should agree at all needs its own ruling」 (`objectstack-ai/objectui#9568`). `percent ⇒ 0` is therefore the value five of six faces already hold, not a new number.
- **number — INCONSISTENT, and one arm is load-bearing.** The cell renderer resolves absence to "no fixed width" while the summary footer and the metric widget resolve it to `0`. Worse, the display-grouping policy keys on the very distinction a default would erase: `packages/core/src/utils/number-display.ts:150-155` is `shouldGroupDisplayNumber(scale) => scale !== 0`, with its own comment 「Only an explicitly declared scale of 0 is an ordinal. `undefined !== 0`」. A DECLARED `scale: 0` marks a discrete integer (a year, a fiscal period, an ordinal) and renders ungrouped; an absent `scale` means "decimals unknown" and keeps its separators. Declaring `number ⇒ 0` would print `2026` where the platform shows `2,026`, for every undeclared number field in the product.
- **currency — the money faces do not read this key at all.** `CurrencyCellRenderer` formats through `formatCurrency(value, currency, locale)` with no `scale`; `CurrencyField` reads `precision` and says so in-line ("No `scale` passed"); fraction digits otherwise come from the currency's own ISO 4217 minor-unit count. The one `2` that looks like a currency default is `GridField.tsx:321`, and it belongs to the inline grid COLUMN surface rounding a computed result — a different schema, as the table above records.

⛔ Neither reading argues for `0` and neither argues for the other face's value. They argue that nobody has ruled yet. Filed as a finding for the seat, ⛔ not guessed here.

## Tests

`packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.test.ts` — 12 cases: the ruled value; a declaration beating it; a declared `0` staying a declaration; `number`/`currency` answering `undefined` with the census reason in-line; the malformed-declaration door (`2.5`, `-1`, `'2'`, `NaN`) matching the one the write path already applies; an over-ceiling width returned verbatim with no second clamp policy; the per-type table held equal to `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` in both directions so a new numeric family member reds until judged; the parse-output pin above; and two describe pins so the ③ facet cannot be trimmed away silently.

**Reverse verification — the direction was predicted as RED before the run, and RED is what it did.** Run from the committed state, mutation proved on disk by blob hash, both legs printed:

```
anchor   "percent: 0,"  x1 -> x0          (declared 1 hit, 1 replaced)
replace  "percent: 2,"  x0 -> x1
blob     9a4fb39378f75d0c0cfe79fa2b42ded3f65d6575 -> d92b3a45a8d657ec5828e7b4cfead261056c53ea

BEFORE   12 passed (12)
AFTER     4 failed | 8 passed (12)
           x resolves an absent scale on a percent field to 0 - the ruled value
           x refuses a malformed declaration through the same door the write path uses
           x holds the per-type table equal to the numeric family in BOTH directions
           x parses a bare percent field to output carrying no `scale` key

restore  blob == HEAD (9a4fb39378f7), `git diff HEAD` empty
```

No `dist` preflight leg: the subject is imported relatively (`import { resolveFieldScale } from './field-scale'`), so the package `exports`/`dist` is not on this suite's resolution path and a stale build cannot produce a false green here. Nothing permanent was left behind — the tree is clean and the mutation is not in any commit.

## Gate readings — taken at `f572bd4ede`, the final commit

Exit codes captured before any pipe. Green:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **510 files / 14916 passed, 1 todo**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — clean (this is `tsc --noEmit` + `check:scripts-typecheck` + `check:test-typecheck`). Measured with `--listFiles`: the BUILD program deliberately excludes `**/*.test.ts`, so the new test is covered by the test-layer program instead — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` contains `field-scale.test.ts`, and `check:test-typecheck` holds at 53 files / 257 errors / 142 pinned signatures, i.e. the new test contributed zero debt.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — all 15 artifacts current after `--fix` regenerated exactly the 3 it proved stale (`api-surface/`, `export-origins/`, `content/docs/references/**`), written from a `dist` that run built, then re-checked
- `pnpm lint` — the **full** repo scan (`eslint . --no-inline-config`), exit 0, 66s. Not narrowed, so no narrowing needs proving.
- 60 further gate families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` and re-derived after the changeset existed, all green, including `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:export-origins`, `check:exported-any`, `check:dual-source-exports`, `check:entry-nameability`, `check:browser-reachable-entries`, `check:liveness`, `check:empty-state`, `check:llms-txt`, `check:variant-docs`, `check:skill-examples`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:yaml-examples`, `check:strictness-ledger`, `check:duration-unit-keys`, `check:objectui-pin-citations`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:published-files`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:issue-citations`, `check:merge-driver`, `check:pm-widening-tells`, `check:pm-prior-rulings`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors`, `check-undeclared-dep-imports`, `check-closing-keyword-parity`, `check-comment-mask-adoption`, `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-keyed-text-bounds`, `check-ci-filter-parity`, and the docs family (`check:doc-anchors`, `check:docs-single-h1`, `check:docs-redirects`, `check:docs-spec-enumerations`, `check:quick-reference-counts`, `check:corpus-claim-drift`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`, `check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:role-word`, `check:published-readme-links`, `check-doc-frontmatter`, `check-docs-section-name`, `check-section-landing-index`, `check-doc-route-spelling --advisory`, `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `docs-audit/check-affected-docs`, `docs-audit/check-drift-comment`).

**NOT MEASURED**, each with its reason — ⛔ neither a pass nor a failure:

- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3): its `--re-measure` leg needs the whole workspace built (`turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`), which does not fit a foreground run here. Its sibling `check:type-check-coverage` is green, and this diff adds no package and no `typecheck` script, so no ledger number is in play. Declared to CI.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3): reads built output for 34 packages with no `dist` in this worktree; needs a full `pnpm build`. Declared to CI (`Build Core`).
- Two other families first read exit 3 for a missing dependency's `dist` and were converted into real readings by building that closure: `check:lean-entry-closure` (after `@objectstack/objectql...`) and `check:docs-transcript-drift` (after `@objectstack/lint...`), both then green.
- CI-only populations the derivation names and no local invocation covers: the `check-shard-attestation` / `check-test-completeness` argv that take a runner variable, the 11 wide-population families, the 52 artifact-roster families, and the 5 path-scheduled CI jobs.

## Declared deviations

- **File surface.** The claim's surface is `packages/spec/src/data/ · packages/spec/json-schema/ · packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ · packages/spec/authorable-surface/ · content/docs/ · .changeset/`. It does not name `packages/spec/api-surface/` or `packages/spec/export-origins/`, and this PR writes both. They are the **mandatory generated consequence** of the two new exports: `check:api-surface` and `check:export-origins` red without them, `TypeScript Type Check` is required and has no paths filter, and both files were written by `check:generated --fix` rather than by hand — their whole diff is two added lines each, naming only `resolveFieldScale` and `FieldScaleMeta`. Stopping instead would have shipped a knowingly red PR for a mechanical artifact. Reported rather than silently taken. `packages/spec/json-schema/`, `authorable-defaults/` and `authorable-surface/` are in the surface and are unchanged.
- **Clause ② re-judged from this diff — same letter, different reason.** The claim's `yes` rests on a `.default()` making the parse payload carry `scale`. This PR adds no default, so that reasoning does not apply to what actually landed. `yes` still holds, on the other limb the repo has already measured: two new exported symbols land on the `@objectstack/spec/data` index, and `pr-automation.yml`'s WHICH LEVEL prose makes "a new exported symbol on an `index`" at least `minor`, while `packages/spec/src/shared/scale-ceiling.ts`'s own docblock prices promoting a constant onto that same surface as 「a new export (`Clause-②: yes`, at least `minor`, and a contract-tier review)」. So the verdict is unchanged and the changeset grades `minor`; only the sentence justifying it moves. Flagged for the seat rather than worked around — a `Clause-②-correction:` is the seat's to write, and none is needed here.
- **Labels: zero writes.** The dispatch names no label and `skip-changeset` does not apply (this PR publishes and carries a changeset), so the writable set is empty.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/spec/src/shared/scale-ceiling.ts` still describes itself as exporting nothing to consumers, and `field.zod.ts` still keeps its own private copies of `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE` / `SCALE_UPPER_BOUND_MESSAGE` — that module's docblock names the delete-and-import as future work owned elsewhere. Untouched here; noted, not filed.
- `packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts:468` in the sibling composes `(col as any).scale ?? meta?.scale` — a column-over-field precedence, not an absent-value default, so it is a different key from the ones the ruling closes. It belongs to the consumer half's reading, ⛔ not to this one.
- `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale` has no declared absent value and needs none today: its `type` enum carries no `percent`, and the one consumer fallback on that surface (`GridField.tsx:321`, `?? (c.type === 'currency' ? 2 : undefined)`) is a rounding policy for a computed value rather than a display width. Noted so a later reader does not mistake the silence for an oversight.
